nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration/testing fees and sandbox costs

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog point sizing and rate-card modeling only.
Story points mapped to hours using a rough baseline of ~7-8 hours/point for backend/frontend work, adjusted per task complexity, then reconciled to role capacity.
1 point ≈ 6-9 hours depending on discipline mix (dev vs QA vs devops); legacy migration (PW-8) and multi-currency (PW-14) assumed higher effort per point due to integration/data risk.

Backend Developer is the primary implementation role for PW-3, PW-4, PW-7, PW-8, PW-9, PW-10, PW-14, PW-17, PW-21 and shares work on most other backend-touching tickets; at 1.5 FTE (~240 hrs/month/dev pair) the 1040 allocated hours implies roughly 4.3 months of full team throughput, which is tight given the backlog breadth — flagged as a capacity risk.

Frontend Developer is a single 1.0 FTE; 760 hours (~4.75 months at full utilization) is fully committed across PW-2, PW-5, PW-6, PW-13, PW-15, PW-18, PW-19, PW-20 plus UI portions of auth/RBAC/2FA — this role is the likely critical-path bottleneck.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (~96 hrs/month) accumulates 420 hours (~4.4 months); QA effort concentrated on payment, RBAC, GDPR and migration correctness given compliance/financial risk.

DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE (~64 hrs/month) accumulates 190 hours (~3 months); scoped to CI/staging setup (PW-1), observability (PW-22), rate limiting/infra hardening (PW-21) and legacy decommission (PW-24) support.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for third-party services (Stripe fees, migration tooling licenses, cloud infra, external accessibility audit) since no vendor quotes were supplied.
Estimate assumes backlog is delivered sequentially by priority (Urgent/High first) with Medium/Low priority items being the first candidates for descoping if budget or timeline pressure emerges.
Pessimistic scenario accounts for the high uncertainty inherent in PW-8 (legacy data migration) and PW-14 (multi-currency), which are historically prone to scope creep.
Optimistic scenario assumes no major integration surprises with Stripe or the legacy Oracle schema and that the design system (PW-2) accelerates later UI tickets more than modeled.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized by mapping backlog story points to role hours, weighting each ticket by which roles it primarily touches (e.g., payment integration and RBAC lean heavily on Backend + QA; design system and responsive layout lean on Frontend; CI/observability/decommission lean on DevOps). Total points across the backlog (198) were distributed across disciplines based on typical Angular/API/SaaS portal effort ratios (roughly 45% backend, 33% frontend, 15% QA, 7% devops), then converted to hours and cross-checked against each role's FTE capacity to flag bottlenecks. Backend Developer and Frontend Developer are the most heavily loaded and constrain the timeline; QA and DevOps are comparatively thin given their lower FTE allocation, so their hours were kept tightly scoped to the highest-risk items (payments, compliance, migration, pipeline). The Most Likely total reflects the sum of these labour lines plus modest non-labour costs for third-party services. Optimistic and Pessimistic scenarios were set at roughly -11%/+15% around the Most Likely total to reflect integration and migration risk without contradicting the underlying line items. Priority breakdown apportions the total cost across Urgent/High/Medium/Low backlog items in proportion to their story points and role costs, to make trade-off conversations easier.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 pts) to a follow-on phase; support staff can use direct DB/read-only tooling short-term.
reductions.effect: Removes largest Low-priority item; primarily reduces Backend + Frontend hours.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics/reporting, Low priority, 8 pts) and PW-23 (Contract tests vs helpdesk API, Low priority, 5 pts) to a post-launch backlog.
reductions.effect: Cuts Backend and QA hours tied to non-critical low-priority tickets.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer allocation on low-risk, low-priority tickets (PW-12, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) and rely on developer self-testing plus lighter regression coverage.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~60 QA hours from low-priority items only; compliance/payment QA coverage untouched.

reductions.description: Defer third-party accessibility audit (PW-15) and rely on internal accessibility checklist/manual review for launch, scheduling the external audit post-launch.
reductions.effect: Removes non-labour external audit cost; adds residual accessibility risk until audit occurs.

reductions.description: Phase Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) into a two-stage rollout: migrate active accounts first, defer historical/inactive invoice-line migration by 1-2 months.
reductions.effect: Reduces near-term Backend + DevOps hours and migration tooling spend; remaining data migrated in a later, separately budgeted phase.
